legend: Denis is a student and he's failed his data security exam, so today he's having a retake. He woke up late and decided to take a taxi.

Denis lives in a city, which can be represented as n$$$n$$$ crossroads connected by m$$$m$$$ bidirectional roads. For every road it is known, how much it takes to drive along it. Denis lives near a crossroad with number s$$$s$$$ and the university is near crossroad t$$$t$$$. As soon as the taxi is near the university, Denis immediately leaves it and rushes for his exam.

Unfortunately, everything is a bit more complicated — hackers had hacked a GPS in Denis's taxi. When the GPS works properly, it helps you to reach your destination as fast, as it's possible. On every crossroad it shows, which road should be taken in order to finish your journey in the fastest way. If there are more than one possible road, GPS can show you any. Hackers can make GPS show you any road they want, but no more than once.

Denis doesn't remember exactly, how did he get to the university, but he remembers the time L$$$L$$$ the road took. It turned out that his teacher had already known about the attack on GPS, so he asked Denis to calculate the number of different possible routes from his place to the university as a part of his retake.

Help Denis calculate the number of routes from crossroad s$$$s$$$ to crossroad t$$$t$$$, that took L$$$L$$$ time and were possible considering the GPS hack. As this number might be very large, find it modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ — number of crossroads and roads between them in the city, where Denis lives (2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$, 1≤m≤min(2⋅105,n(n−1)2)$$$1 \leq m \leq \min{(2 \cdot 10^5, \frac{n(n - 1)}{2})}$$$).

The second line contains three integers s$$$s$$$, t$$$t$$$ and L$$$L$$$ — crossroad number, where Denis lives, number of the crossroad near the university and the ride time (1≤s,t≤n$$$1 \leq s, t \leq n$$$, s≠t$$$s \neq t$$$, 1≤L≤2⋅1014$$$1 \leq L \leq 2 \cdot 10^{14}$$$).

The next m$$$m$$$ lines contain descriptions of roads between crossroads. The description contains three integers v$$$v$$$, u$$$u$$$, w$$$w$$$ (1≤v,u≤n$$$1 \leq v, u \leq n$$$, v≠u$$$v \neq u$$$, 1≤w≤109$$$1 \leq w \leq 10^9$$$) — numbers of the two crossroads connected by this road and the time, needed to drive along it.

All the roads are bidirectional, any pair of crossroads is connected with no more than one road. No roads connect a crossroad with itself. It is guaranteed that it is possible to get from crossroad s$$$s$$$ to the crossroad t$$$t$$$.
output: Print the only integer — number of routes Denis could have modulo 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$.

legend.ai: Denis 是一名学生，他的数据安全考试没及格，所以今天要补考。他起床晚了，决定打车去。
Denis 所在的城市可以表示成有 n$$$n$$$ 个路口、由 m$$$m$$$ 条双向道路连接。每条道路都知道开车通过需要多长时间。Denis 住在编号为 s$$$s$$$ 的路口附近，大学在编号为 t$$$t$$$ 的路口附近。出租车一靠近大学，Denis 就立刻下车冲向考场。
不幸的是，事情要更复杂一些——黑客入侵了 Denis 出租车上的 GPS。GPS 正常工作时，会帮助你尽可能快地到达目的地。它在每个路口显示为了以最快方式走完全程应该走哪条路。如果有多条可选道路，GPS 可以显示其中任意一条。黑客可以让 GPS 显示他们想要的任意一条道路，但这种篡改最多只能发生一次。
Denis 记不清自己具体是怎么到大学的，但他记得这段路程用了 L$$$L$$$ 时间。原来他的老师已经知道 GPS 被攻击的事，所以老师让 Denis 计算从家到大学有多少条不同的可能路线，作为补考的一部分。
请帮助 Denis 计算从路口 s$$$s$$$ 到路口 t$$$t$$$ 的路线数量，这些路线耗时恰好为 L$$$L$$$，并且在 GPS 被攻击的情况下是有可能发生的。由于这个数字可能非常大，请输出它对 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$ 取模的结果。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n$$$n$$$ 和 m$$$m$$$——Denis 所在城市的路口数量以及路口之间的道路数量(2≤n≤2⋅105$$$2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$，1≤m≤min(2⋅105,n(n−1)2)$$$1 \leq m \leq \min{(2 \cdot 10^5, \frac{n(n - 1)}{2})}$$$)。
第二行包含三个整数 s$$$s$$$、t$$$t$$$ 和 L$$$L$$$，分别表示十字路口的编号、Denis 居住的十字路口编号、大学附近的十字路口编号以及乘车时间(1≤s,t≤n$$$1 \leq s, t \leq n$$$，s≠t$$$s \neq t$$$，1≤L≤2⋅1014$$$1 \leq L \leq 2 \cdot 10^{14}$$$)。
接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行描述十字路口之间的道路。每行包含三个整数 v$$$v$$$、u$$$u$$$、w$$$w$$$(1≤v,u≤n$$$1 \leq v, u \leq n$$$，v≠u$$$v \neq u$$$，1≤w≤109$$$1 \leq w \leq 10^9$$$)，分别表示这条道路连接的两个十字路口编号，以及沿着这条道路行驶所需的时间。
所有道路都是双向的，任意两个十字路口之间至多有一条道路。没有道路连接某个十字路口和自身。保证可以从十字路口 s$$$s$$$ 到达十字路口 t$$$t$$$。

output.ai: 输出唯一一个整数，即 Denis 可以选择的路线数量对 109+7$$$10^9 + 7$$$ 取模的结果。
